ereader.title: Modern System Architecture & e-Reader Reference Guide
ereader.author: Exam App Engineering Team

sections.title: 1. Introduction & Architecture Vision
sections.text:
This document is a comprehensive technical reference volume engineered to validate all visual, functional, and **heading depth (TOC hierarchy)** capabilities of the standalone **Exam App** e-Reader engine.

> [!abstract] Scope and Objective
> This volume allows you to evaluate multi-tier heading depth (from Level 1 down to Level 4), Obsidian callouts, multi-column aligned data tables, syntax-highlighted code blocks, and page-based (`unit: "page"`) pagination in a unified specimen.

### Why a Standalone Reader?
Reading long technical manuals inside question/flashcard drills often fractures concentration. The e-Reader provides an isolated environment free of distracting exam metrics.

- [x] Completely isolated reading environment
- [x] Multi-level collapsible Table of Contents (TOC)
- [x] Persistent reading position and progress tracking

sections.title: 1.1 Core Architecture & Isolation Model
sections.text:
The e-Reader engine is strictly isolated from the application's central state machine. This architectural boundary ensures high performance and data integrity.

> [!info] Autonomous Lifecycle
> The reader repository is not loaded during initial application bootstrap; it initializes asynchronously only when the user navigates into the library for the first time.

sections.title: 1.1.1 Standalone Reading vs. Test Center
sections.text:
Reading durations, viewed pages, or highlighted passages do not alter **FSRS spaced-repetition parameters**, card due dates, or active streak counters.

> [!note] Focus Principle
> Reading mode is dedicated to undisturbed, deep source-material immersion.

```text
[Test Center]     <-- Zero Data Coupling -->     [e-Reader Engine]
  - FSRS Cards                                      - Page Navigation
  - Exam Scores                                     - Notes & Highlights
  - Streak Counters                                 - Deep TOC Tree
```

sections.title: 1.1.1.1 State Management & Memory Efficiency
sections.text:
This sub-section explicitly tests **Level 4 heading depth** and nested indentation (`--toc-depth: 3`) in the Table of Contents.

> [!tip] Performance Tip
> To avoid DOM bloat, the reader renders only the active chapter and its immediate neighborhood.

Key memory management tenets:
1. Strict DOM node constraints
2. Passive scroll listener attachments
3. Lifecycle cleanup upon chapter transitions

sections.title: 1.1.2 Persistence & Storage Synchronization
sections.text:
Book contents and bookmark positions reside securely in browser-local **IndexedDB** and **localStorage** layers.

> [!success] Seamless Resumption
> Reopening the application days later instantly positions you back at the exact line and chapter you last read.

sections.title: 1.2 Typography, Pagination & Visual Layout
sections.text: Line length, character tracking, and contrast ratios follow modern accessibility guidelines to minimize eye strain during extended reading sessions.

sections.title: 1.2.1 Dynamic Font Scaling & Preferences
sections.text:
The header controls provide `A-` and `A+` buttons for live font adjustment.

- `A-`: Step-decreases the font size.
- `A+`: Step-increases the font size.
- The selected scale remains ==persistent== across sessions.

> [!example] CSS Variable Injection
> The font size scales instantly via the `var(--ereader-font-size, 1.05rem)` custom property.

sections.title: 1.2.2 Media & Responsive Image Integration
sections.text:
The reader engine safely embeds remote media delivered over secure `https://` protocols.

![Software Architecture Workspace](https://images.pexels.com/photos/1181675/pexels-photo-1181675.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=800)

Illustrations are centered and responsive, preventing text distortion across varying viewports.

The box below is an **empty image placeholder**: the AI never inserts figures itself; it leaves a placeholder with the caption, a short description and the page instead. Tap the box to add the picture from your device or by link — a link is saved into the book, a picture from your device stays on this device only.

![Figure 1.2 Reader layout overview | Diagram: header with search on top, contents list on the left, reading area in the middle | p. 3](placeholder:fig-1-2)

sections.title: 2. Obsidian Markdown & Rich Content Specification
sections.text:
Exam App adheres to **100% native Obsidian Markdown**. No raw HTML markup is evaluated; rich formatting relies entirely on standard Markdown syntax.

> [!abstract] Chapter Overview
> This chapter thoroughly tests callout styles, multi-column tables, fenced code blocks, and inline decorations.

sections.title: 2.1 Obsidian Callout Taxonomy
sections.text: Obsidian `> [!type] Title` syntax highlights focal information. The reader recognizes and formats 11 canonical styles.

sections.title: 2.1.1 Informational & Summary Boxes
sections.text:
The following blocks verify standard informational callouts:

> [!note] Standard Note Block
> Used for auxiliary background context and explanatory remarks.

> [!info] System Information
> The engine operates with zero runtime external dependencies.

> [!abstract] Executive Summary (TL;DR)
> Lightweight parsing ensures swift document startup times.

sections.title: 2.1.2 Warning, Failure & Success Admonitions
sections.text:
Validating error and caution indicators:

> [!tip] Best Practice Tip
> Authoring headings in strict hierarchical order (`Level 1 -> Level 2 -> Level 3`) ensures seamless TOC folding.

> [!success] Pipeline Verification
> Test suites executed with zero failures and verified schema integrity.

> [!warning] Security Precaution
> Raw HTML tags (`div`, `span`) are safely escaped and emitted as plain text.

> [!danger] Critical Safety Warning
> Clearing local browser cache without cloud sync resets uncommitted bookmarks.

sections.title: 2.1.3 Case Studies, Hints & Quotations
sections.text:

sections.title: 3. Navigation, In-Book Search & Metrics
sections.text: Swift navigation across chapters, rapid keyword location, and effortless orientation within the outline tree represent the core value of the reading engine.

sections.title: 3.1 Collapsible Table of Contents (TOC)
sections.text:
Top-level headings with sub-chapters display an expandable chevron toggle in the left navigation drawer.

> [!tip] How to Test
> 1. Click the menu button in the header to open the **Contents** drawer.
> 2. Click the chevron toggle beside `1. Introduction` or `2. Obsidian Markdown`.
> 3. Observe the child sub-chapters collapsing and expanding smoothly.
> 4. Verify that `Level 4` items carry distinctive visual indentation (`--toc-depth`).

sections.title: 3.2 Real-Time In-Book Search & Highlights
sections.text:
Open the in-book search bar to locate keywords across sections.

> [!question] Recommended Search Terms
> Try searching for the following keywords to test multiple occurrences and match navigation:
> - `architecture` (Locates occurrences across chapters)
> - `callout` (Found across multiple admonitions)
> - `depth` (Dispersed in hierarchy test sections)
> - `level` (Appears across TOC specifications)
